Yesterday, the U.S. government announced an update to its list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotics equipment." Today, a spokesperson for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed that the ban also applies to robotic vacuum cleaners.

The robotic vacuum ban affects popular brands such as Roomba and Roborock, but you can continue to use your existing products.

When the Trump administration announced yesterday that "advanced robotics equipment" would be banned from entering the U.S., headlines focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't necessarily require legs—and neither does the FCC's robotics ban. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's director of media relations, confirmed to The Verge that the ban will also cover robotic vacuums. Existing Roombas are not affected, and already-approved models can continue to be imported and sold. However, the government claims that future foreign-made robots will pose national security risks, and even robotic vacuum companies are being required to commit to manufacturing in the United States.

The FCC considers advanced robotics equipment to carry national security risks—a logic that applies equally to products most people consider harmless, such as robotic vacuums and smart lawnmowers.

Unless explicitly approved, or manufactured domestically in the U.S., they may not be sold in the country.

This ban is particularly devastating to the robotic vacuum market, as major brands including Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own these products, you can continue using them for now without interference—the FCC won't be showing up to confiscate your robotic vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban is enforced, the robotic vacuum market could see dramatic changes in the foreseeable future. If all of this sounds familiar, it's because it mirrors the ban on wireless routers that was imposed just months ago.

Will you continue using your existing robotic vacuum? Why or why not? Share your thoughts in the comments.
